entries.title: Sleep and Circadian Rhythm
entries.summary: Los cambios de sueño y ritmos circadianos reducen la vigilancia, aumentan la fatiga, empeoran la velocidad de reacción y pueden afectar la cognición en misiones largas.
excerpts: Sleep loss and circadian disruption reduce alertness, slow reaction time and can impair performance during long-duration missions.
Crewmembers should prioritize sleep opportunity, light exposure management and fatigue countermeasures to preserve mission performance.

entries.title: Cardiovascular and Behavioral Health
entries.summary: Mantener la salud cardiovascular y la respuesta al estrés es esencial durante misiones espaciales; la tolerancia al estrés y la recuperación influencian la seguridad operativa.
excerpts: Cardiovascular deconditioning, stress and altered autonomic regulation must be tracked to protect crew performance and decision making.
Behavioral health countermeasures should monitor stress, workload, recovery and interpersonal factors during long missions.

entries.title: Vision and Visual Function
entries.summary: La salud visual y la respuesta ocular deben revisarse si aparecen cambios de visión, fatiga visual o molestias de enfoque durante la misión.
excerpts: Eye and visual changes can affect task performance and should be monitored when symptoms appear during spaceflight.
Symptoms such as blurred vision, eye strain and visual discomfort warrant evaluation alongside workload and recovery context.

entries.title: Environmental Health and Air Quality
entries.summary: La calidad ambiental, la ventilación y el nivel de CO₂ afectan la vigilancia mental, la concentración y la respuesta cognitiva.
excerpts: Environmental controls and air quality matter because elevated CO₂ and cabin stressors can affect crew alertness and performance.
Mission monitors should pay attention to ventilation, contamination risk and symptoms that relate to mental clarity or productivity.
